quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When visibility is poor, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slowing down is the first thing you should do when visibility is poor or road conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. What should drivers know?

options.text: Drivers have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians can safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians who are in a crosswalk.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When another car is on your left at an unmarked intersection and you arrive at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians who are on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing with no traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will not happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching an unmarked railroad crossing. Check both directions for trains before crossing. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance from the nearest track and wait until the train passes.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road right away.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right side of the road when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
No U-turn.
Yield.
Do not enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It means you cannot continue driving in your current direction.

questions.question: What technique helps avoid crashes when driving on ice or snow?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better traction.
Leave the highway as quickly as possible.
Turn on four-wheel drive.
Slow down and increase your distance from other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and increase your distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on snowy or icy roads. Slowing down and keeping more distance from other vehicles are the most important ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: You want to turn left at a green light, but traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Take your turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left and there is oncoming traffic, wait for it to pass before you turn. If the light is green and no other car ahead of you is turning left, you can enter the intersection to prepare for your turn.

questions.question: In good driving conditions, what is the minimum safe distance to keep behind another vehicle?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
10 seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: Use the Three-Second-Plus rule. When the car ahead of you passes an object, count three seconds before your car reaches the same object. If you reach it sooner, you are following too closely. Keep more distance in poor conditions.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
Look ahead and stay a safe distance behind other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and stay a safe distance behind other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems ahead without sudden stops. Emergency stops can cause the car behind you to crash into you.

questions.question: What should drivers do to avoid carbon monoxide poisoning?

options.text: Have your exhaust system checked regularly for leaks.
Keep your engine off when parked in an enclosed garage.
Close vents when driving close behind another car.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide is a deadly, odorless gas. Signs of poisoning include sudden tiredness, yawning, dizziness, and nausea. Fresh air is the only cure.

questions.question: When do roads freeze quickly?

options.text: On flat roads.
On curvy roads.
In sunny areas.
In shaded areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: In shaded areas.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be extra careful on roads shaded by trees or buildings. These areas freeze faster than other parts of the road and are the last to dry.

questions.question: What must you do when driving near a motorcycle?

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle share half a lane.
Pass the motorcycle while sharing its lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give motorcyclists a complete lane so they have room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: A five-ounce glass of wine has the same amount of alcohol as:

options.text: One pint of whiskey.
A gallon of wine.
A six-pack of beer.
One 12-ounce can of beer.

questions.correctAnswerText: One 12-ounce can of beer.
questions.explanation: Beer, wine, and whiskey contain about the same amount of alcohol in standard servings. A five-ounce glass of wine (12% alcohol), a 12-ounce can of beer, and 1.5 ounces of 86-proof liquor all have roughly the same alcohol content. The type of drink does not matter—the same amount of alcohol impairs driving equally.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: No matter what direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter what direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: You must pull to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is behind you or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal works the same as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: At a flashing red signal, you must stop and let all other traffic pass.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a busy intersection and cannot see past oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up quickly as soon as the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you through.
Inch forward into each lane as traffic clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and safe to enter.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal, you should:

options.text: Merge in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Go ahead—oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive at the posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Stay close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When rain reduces how far you can see, reduce your speed. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If rain is too heavy to see clearly, pull to the shoulder and stop until it improves.

questions.question: At a yield sign, what should you do?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop before entering.
Yield only to traffic on your right.
Yield only to traffic on your left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other traffic pass first before you enter the intersection or roadway.

questions.question: When must you turn on your headlights while driving?

options.text: When you turn on your wipers.
One half hour after sunset.
One half hour before sunrise.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights from one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise. Also use them when you cannot see 500 feet ahead and anytime your wipers are on.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop completely. Running a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if there is no sign prohibiting it.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing in front of your car. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass ahead of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful around children. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way in crosswalks.

questions.question: How should small children ride in a vehicle?

options.text: They can be held safely by an adult.
They are safe standing on the floor in the back.
They will not get hurt because they are small.
They must be in a proper car seat and never standing.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must be in a proper car seat and never standing.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats designed for their size. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always use a proper car seat for children.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with no signs or signals at the same time as a car on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through first.
Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and make the other car stop.
Honk your horn and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Wait for that vehicle to pass safely before you proceed.

questions.question: When should you drive slower than the posted speed limit?

options.text: When road or weather conditions are not perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When road or weather conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive slower when roads are wet, visibility is poor, or any condition is not ideal. You can get a ticket for speeding even if you are within the posted limit if the conditions are bad.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you has flashing red lights. What must you do?

options.text: Stop at least 25 feet away.
Slow down to 10 mph.
Speed up and pass the bus.
Stop directly behind the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at least 25 feet away.
questions.explanation: When a school bus flashes red lights, stop at least 25 feet away. The only exception is if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway. Then, slow to 10 mph.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes immediately.
Hold the steering wheel firmly and slowly stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slowly stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake hard if a tire blows out. Grip the wheel tightly and stay in your lane. Release the gas slowly and brake gently once you are going very slowly. Then pull to a safe area.

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?

options.text: On the main road just before the exit.
When you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane well ahead of where you need to exit. Wait until you are in the exit lane before you slow down.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Slowly slow down and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the gas and do not brake immediately. Slowly reduce your speed, then gently apply the brakes and pull off the road.

questions.question: What does a "No stopping" sign mean?

options.text: You can stop long enough to unload packages.
You can stop to avoid hitting another vehicle.
You can stop to drop off passengers.
You can stop for less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop to avoid hitting another vehicle.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, follow a police officer's direction, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: What do pentagon-shaped signs mean?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagon-shaped signs show you are in a school zone. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians near schools.

questions.question: A car is driving toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: If another car is coming at you head-on, honk to get the driver's attention. If they don't move, steer to the right. Steering left is dangerous because if the other driver swerves at the last moment, you will still crash. Brake hard and steady. Slowing down even slightly will reduce the impact.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Use the rearview mirror inside the car.
Use the side mirror outside the car.
Use both the inside and outside mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spots before every lane change.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road is getting wider.
The right lane is ending soon.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.
The left lane is ending soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending soon.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the right lane will end soon.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in rain?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: What happens when you drive while distracted?

options.text: It is never dangerous.
You react slower to dangers on the road.
You usually drive faster.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You react slower to dangers on the road.
questions.explanation: Distractions make drivers slower to react to traffic and road hazards. Distracted driving is always unsafe.

questions.question: What does NOT affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Physical fitness does not affect BAC.

questions.question: You are angry after a work problem. What should you do before driving home?

options.text: Play loud radio so you don't think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to release stress.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Stop at a bar for drinks before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, take time to calm down before driving. Letting anger out while driving is dangerous to you and others.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines double in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare drivers for hazards ahead. This sign warns you about low clearance.

questions.question: Why is a space cushion between your vehicle and others important?

options.text: Prevents distractions from other vehicles.
Allows you time to react to unexpected situations.
Keeps traffic flowing at a safe pace.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Space between vehicles gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive carefully through the intersection.
Prepare to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly and carefully. Look both ways before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Steep downgrade.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you about a steep hill ahead. Slow down to avoid brake damage or collision.

questions.question: A transit bus is signaling to enter a traffic lane ahead of you. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly pass the bus before it re-enters traffic.
Yield the right-of-way to the transit bus.
Expect the bus to yield the right-of-way to you.
Either yield the right-of-way or don't yield the right-of-way. There is no specific rule.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to the transit bus.
questions.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way when a transit bus signals to enter your lane. Slow down or change lanes to help the bus merge safely.

questions.question: Which behavior shows a driver is aggressive?

options.text: Fail to properly yield the right-of-way.
Maintain a three-second following distance.
Never change traffic lanes.
Are driving with a burned out headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fail to properly yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Aggressive drivers make dangerous decisions like erratic lane changes, following too closely, and failing to yield. Avoid confronting them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks only.
Trucks are entering the highway.
Upcoming hill.
Trucks have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming hill.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow backgrounds. This sign warns you about a steep hill ahead. Adjust your speed for safe driving.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Through shallow water.
More quickly.
More slowly.
Through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down to reduce the risk.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating.
Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.
Look right first, then left, then right again.
Look left first, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left first, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then left again in case you missed any traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
An upcoming curve in the road.
Changes in traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: An upcoming curve in the road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves to the right ahead.
